common_name: Evelyn Rose (Apricot David Austin English Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Evelyn is famous for its rich fruity fragrance, which was licensed for use in Crabtree & Evelyn perfumes and toiletries.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Introduced by David Austin in 1991, Evelyn bears large, fully double, peony-like blooms in warm apricot-peach with an exceptionally rich, fruity fragrance reminiscent of ripe apricots and fresh peaches, a scent so distinctive it was licensed to the British fragrance house Crabtree & Evelyn for a signature line of perfumes and toiletries. It reblooms in flushes from late spring through fall on a vigorous, well-branched shrub. Prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain repeat flowering.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: Sharifa Asma Rose (Soft Pink David Austin English Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Sharifa Asma bears soft, pale pink, cupped, myrrh-scented blooms on a relatively compact, well-branched shrub.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Introduced by David Austin in 1989, Sharifa Asma bears delicate, soft blush-pink, shallowly cupped double blooms with a strong myrrh fragrance, opening on a compact, well-branched shrub that fits smaller beds and mixed borders. Its gentle color and refined flower form have made it a long-standing favorite among softer-toned English roses. It reblooms in flushes from late spring through fall; prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and provide good air circulation to help manage black spot in humid conditions.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: Tamora Rose (Fragrant Apricot-Orange David Austin English Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Tamora is a compact David Austin rose known for one of the strongest myrrh fragrances in the entire English rose line.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Introduced by David Austin in 1983, Tamora bears small, cupped, apricot-orange double blooms carrying one of the strongest, most distinctive myrrh fragrances of any English rose, a scent many gardeners find unlike any other rose class. Its compact, bushy habit fits foundation beds and small borders well. It reblooms in flushes from late spring through fall; prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and provide good air circulation to help manage black spot in humid, rainy conditions.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: Winchester Cathedral Rose (White Sport of Mary Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Winchester Cathedral is a white sport of the pink Mary Rose, sharing the same vigorous, bushy growth habit.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Introduced by David Austin in 1988 as a white-flowered sport of the popular pink Mary Rose, Winchester Cathedral bears the same cupped, informally double flower form in pure white, occasionally showing a faint pink fleck or streak on a petal as a reminder of its parentage, with a light, fresh, old-rose fragrance. It shares Mary Rose's vigorous, bushy, reliable growth habit and reblooms readily in flushes from late spring through fall. Prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain repeat flowering.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: Redouté Rose (Soft Pink David Austin English Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Redouté, named for the celebrated French botanical rose artist, bears clear soft pink, rosette-shaped blooms on a vigorous, upright shrub.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Introduced by David Austin in 1992 and named for Pierre-Joseph Redouté, the celebrated 18th-century botanical artist famous for his rose paintings, this rose bears large, clear soft pink, densely petaled, rosette-shaped blooms with a light, sweet fragrance, opening on a vigorous, reliably upright shrub. Its soft, classic color and shapely flowers have kept it a steady favorite for romantic, cottage-style borders. It reblooms in flushes from late spring through fall; prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: Scepter'd Isle Rose (Fragrant Soft Pink David Austin English Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Scepter'd Isle bears soft pink, cupped, strongly myrrh-scented blooms on an upright, well-branched shrub.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Introduced by David Austin in 1996 and named from a line in Shakespeare's Richard II, Scepter'd Isle bears soft, pale pink, shallowly cupped double blooms with a strong, distinctive myrrh fragrance carried on an upright, well-branched shrub. Its gentle color and pronounced scent have made it a popular choice for fragrance-focused rose gardens. It reblooms in flushes from late spring through fall; prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and provide good air circulation to help manage black spot in humid, rainy conditions.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive
